user.title: Choose the TV
user.description: Select the TV already set up in the LG webOS TV integration. Screen capture uses that connection, so the media player stays connected. Pair separately only for a TV that is not in that list.

manual.title: Connect to an LG webOS TV
manual.description: Enter the TV's IP address. The TV must be on. This pairs with its own key and does not use the media player's connection.

pairing.title: Pair with the TV
pairing.description: Submit, then accept the connection prompt on the TV with the remote. You have about ten seconds.

attach.title: Use the existing LG webOS TV connection
attach.description: This TV is already paired with Home Assistant. Screen capture will share that connection and will not open a second one.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair again
reauth_confirm.description: The TV rejected the saved pairing. Submit, then accept the new prompt on the TV.

reconfigure.title: Update the TV address
reconfigure.description: Change the host if the TV's IP address changed. The existing pairing key is kept.

reconfigure_shared.title: Address follows LG webOS TV
reconfigure_shared.description: This screen uses the LG webOS TV connection. Change the TV's address on that integration. Doing it here would open a second connection.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect. Check the IP address and that the TV is on.
error.error_pairing: The TV rejected pairing. Accept the prompt on the TV and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_in_progress: This TV is already being configured.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the discovered TV.
abort.wrong_device: That address is a different TV.
abort.use_webostv_reauth: This screen uses the LG webOS TV connection. Pair again on that integration.

init.title: Screen capture
init.description: Auto tries the video-plane capture first, which is what includes Netflix, Disney+ and HDMI on webOS 4.10. 960×540 is required on this generation. A flat black frame means the TV withheld that picture.
